provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Experiment planning
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state what an experiment is.
The pupils should be able to list steps in planning an experiment.

Introduction:
We have done many science activities. Today we learn how to plan experiments.

Content:
An experiment is a test to find answers. We ask questions. We make guesses. We test our guesses. We see what happens. For example we can test if beans grow better with water or without water.

Class activity:
Children work in pairs. They think of a simple question like which toy rolls faster. They plan how to test it.

Evaluation questions:
What is an experiment?
What is the first step in planning?
Name one thing we use in experiments.

Summary:
Planning experiments helps us find answers to our questions.

topics.title: Plant experiment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain why plants need water.
The pupils should be able to record plant growth.

Introduction:
Last week we learned about planning experiments. Today we grow plants to see what happens.

Content:
Plants need water to grow. We will test this with two bean plants. One plant gets water every day. The other gets no water. We will measure how tall each plant grows each day using a ruler. We draw the plants in our science books.

Class activity:
Children plant bean seeds in two cups. They water one cup and leave the other dry. They put them near the window.

Evaluation questions:
What do plants need to grow?
Which plant will grow taller? Why?
How do we record growth?

Summary:
Water helps plants grow strong and tall.

topics.title: Weather station
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify rain and wind.
The pupils should be able to record daily weather.

Introduction:
We know the weather changes. Some days it rains. Some days it is windy. Today we make a weather station.

Content:
We can measure rain with a rain gauge. We can see wind with a wind flag. A rain gauge is a container that catches rain. We measure how much rain falls. A wind flag moves when wind blows. We make a chart to write down the weather each day.

Class activity:
Children make a simple wind flag with paper and a stick. They place it outside. They also make a rain gauge with a bottle.

Evaluation questions:
What does a rain gauge do?
What happens to a wind flag in wind?
How many days will we check the weather?

Summary:
Our weather station helps us learn about the weather.

topics.title: Solar oven snack
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain that the sun gives heat.
The pupils should be able to make a simple solar oven.

Introduction:
The sun is hot. It can cook food. Today we use the sun to melt chocolate for a snack.

Content:
The sun gives us heat energy. We can use this energy to cook food. A solar oven is a box that catches sunlight. We put chocolate in the box. The sun's heat melts the chocolate. We can make a simple solar oven with a cardboard box and aluminum foil.

Class activity:
Children help make a solar oven. They place chocolate inside and put it in the sun. They watch as it melts.

Evaluation questions:
What does the sun give us?
What can we make with a solar oven?
What food will we melt today?

Summary:
The sun's heat can cook our snack.

topics.title: Bridge building
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to build a simple bridge.
The pupils should be able to test which bridge is strongest.

Introduction:
We see bridges over rivers and roads. Today we build our own bridges and see which one is strongest.

Content:
A bridge is a structure that goes over something. We can build bridges with sticks and tape. We test bridges by putting weights on them. The bridge that holds the most weight is the strongest. Strong bridges have supports underneath.

Class activity:
Children work in groups to build bridges with ice cream sticks and tape. They test their bridges by placing small objects on top.

Evaluation questions:
What is a bridge?
What materials do we use to build bridges?
How do we test which bridge is strongest?

Summary:
Good bridges are strong and can hold weight.

topics.title: Boat engineering
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to design a boat that floats.
The pupils should be able to test how much cargo a boat can carry.

Introduction:
Boats float on water. Today we design and test our own boats to see how much they can carry.

Content:
Boats float because they are light and water pushes them up. We can make boats from plastic containers. We add cargo like small stones or coins. The boat that can carry the most cargo without sinking is the best boat. Good boats have wide bottoms.

Class activity:
Children make boats from plastic bottles. They test how many coins their boat can carry before it sinks.

Evaluation questions:
Why do boats float?
What makes a boat carry more cargo?
What happens if a boat is too heavy?

Summary:
Good boats are light and have wide bottoms.

topics.title: Sound experiment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to explain how sound travels.
The pupils should be able to make a string telephone.

Introduction:
We hear sounds every day. Today we learn how sound travels by making string telephones.

Content:
Sound travels through the air as vibrations. When we talk our voice makes vibrations. These vibrations travel to our ears. A string telephone shows this. We use two cups and a string. When we talk into one cup the sound travels through the string to the other cup.

Class activity:
Children make string telephones with paper cups and string. They take turns talking and listening through them.

Evaluation questions:
How does sound travel?
What do we use to make a string telephone?
What happens when we pull the string tight?

Summary:
Sound travels as vibrations through materials.

topics.title: Light and colour
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to identify rainbow colours.
The pupils should be able to mix light colours.

Introduction:
We see rainbows after rain. Today we learn about light and how we make colours.

Content:
Light is what helps us see. Sunlight has all colours. When sunlight goes through a prism it makes a rainbow. The rainbow colours are red orange yellow green blue indigo violet. We can mix coloured lights to make new colours. Red and blue light make purple light.

Class activity:
Children use prisms to make rainbows with sunlight. They mix coloured transparent papers to see new colours.

Evaluation questions:
What colours are in a rainbow?
What does a prism do to sunlight?
What colour do red and blue make?

Summary:
Sunlight has all colours and we can mix them.

topics.title: Earth care project
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to list ways to care for the Earth.
The pupils should be able to make an eco poster.

Introduction:
Our Earth needs our care. Today we learn how to reduce reuse and recycle things.

Content:
We can care for Earth by reducing waste. Reuse means using things again like water bottles. Recycle means making new things from old things like paper. We should not litter. We should plant trees. Trees help clean the air.

Class activity:
Children work together to make a poster showing how to care for Earth. They draw pictures of recycling and planting trees.

Evaluation questions:
What does reduce mean?
What can we reuse?
How do trees help us?

Summary:
We must all care for our Earth.

topics.title: Revision and science fair
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to show their science projects.
The pupils should be able to explain what they learned.

Introduction:
Today is our science fair. We show all the things we made and learned this term.

Content:
A science fair is when we show our experiments and projects to others. We display our work on tables. We talk about what we did and what we learned. Parents can come and see our work. We can also see what other children made.

Class activity:
Children set up their projects around the classroom. They take turns explaining their projects to parents and friends.

Evaluation questions:
What is a science fair?
What project are you most proud of?
What did you learn this term?

Summary:
The science fair shows all our hard work and learning.
